methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective descriptive cohort analysis of 5,052 breast cancer patients (2004-2024) at single hospital. Logistic regression analysis of discharge status. Limitations: descriptive epidemiology without control group, selection bias (hospitalized patients only), no molecular subtype data, short-term outcomes (discharge status) used instead of long-term survival.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Descriptive epidemiologic analysis of breast cancer hospitalization patterns in Southern China. Limited clinical applicability; documents trends but no direct guidance for patient management. Relevant for healthcare administration and resource planning at regional level.

reporting_quality.justification: Methods describe study design and data source (hospital administrative system). Results present demographic/clinical characteristics and temporal trends. Logistic regression model described. Limited detail on data quality control, validation procedures. Missing molecular subtype data acknowledged.

novelty_literature.justification: Retrospective trend analysis of breast cancer cases at single hospital. Confirms known epidemiological patterns (peak age 40-59, upper outer quadrant predominance, majority early-stage). Adds regional variation data but no new pathophysiologic insights or clinical discoveries.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear organization with demographic, clinical characteristics, and treatment patterns systematically described. Figures effectively communicate trends (hospitalization surge, LOS reduction, cost evolution). Discussion appropriately contextualizes within Chinese healthcare system changes. Some sections repetitive.

key_strengths: Large single-institution cohort (5,052 patients) with 20-year observation period documenting regional trends
Comprehensive demographic and clinical characteristic documentation
Clear presentation of temporal trends in surgical management and healthcare costs
key_concerns: Purely descriptive epidemiologic analysis without comparison group or causal analysis
Selection bias: hospitalized patients only; outpatient management not captured; likely overrepresents complex/referral cases
Outcomes limited to short-term discharge status (cured/improved/not improved/death) rather than long-term recurrence/survival
Missing molecular subtype data (ER, PR, HER2) limits interpretation of treatment patterns across biologically distinct subgroups
chief_reviewer.rationale: Comprehensive retrospective trend analysis documenting breast cancer management evolution at regional hospital. Limited novelty; confirms established epidemiologic patterns. Lack of long-term outcomes, molecular data, and causal analysis limit scientific and clinical value. Appropriate for health services research or administrative communication but falls below publication threshold for peer-reviewed oncology journals.
